freshness.title: Data freshness
freshness.ageLabel: Age of the latest run per connector against its SLA
freshness.ageNote: Age is hours since the latest raw.sync_run row finished (started, while running). The rule is the {source} SLA of {hours} h: green within SLA + {grace} h grace, amber within 2×SLA, red beyond that, when the latest run failed, or when a run has been running for more than {stale} h. Connectors without a documented schedule are grey and not scored.
freshness.ageNoteNoSla: No connector has a documented schedule, so there is no SLA rule to draw.
freshness.neverRun: never run — no row in raw.sync_run; scheduled every {sla} h, scores 0

freshness.unreadable: latest run could not be read: {reason}
freshness.noBars: no connector has a run to draw

freshness.typedLabel: Row counts of the typed tables, grouped by connector
freshness.typedNote: count(*) per table at the sampled instant. A table missing on this database is listed with its reason, never drawn as zero.
freshness.noTyped: no typed table could be counted
freshness.runsNote: One mark per raw.sync_run row, placed by start time; runs on the same day fan out inside that day. The shape carries the state as well as the colour.

page.title: Time
page.unlinkedTitle: No time-tracking record linked to your account
page.unlinkedBody: Your account isn't linked to a Time Tracking member yet, so there is no personal time to show. That is expected before the first TrackingTime import runs, or if your email doesn't match a tracked user. Switch to Team to see what you're permitted to view, or ask an administrator to link it.
page.emptyBody: Entries appear here once time is tracked or imported from TrackingTime. An empty list can also mean you don't have access to anybody else's time, which is the access model working rather than a fault.

weekSummary.title: Week summary
weekSummary.meta: WEEK OF {week} · {count, plural, one {# MEMBER} other {# MEMBERS}}
weekSummary.note: Calendar time is shown separately because it is mostly synced placeholders rather than deliberate work, and folding it into the total would inflate every utilisation figure here.

tracker.readOnly: Your role permits viewing time but not logging it, so these controls are disabled. That is the access model working rather than a fault.
tracker.utcNote: Times are read in UTC, matching how entries are stored and shown.

actions.notPermitted: Your role does not permit logging time.
actions.noMemberRow: Your account isn't linked to a Time Tracking member yet, so there is nothing to log time against. An administrator can link it.
actions.pickProjectOrTaskTimer: Pick a project or a task before starting the timer.
actions.timerAlreadyRunning: A timer is already running. Stop it before starting another.
actions.clampedAtDay: Timer ran longer than 24 hours and was capped at 24:00. Edit the entry if that isn't right.
actions.invalidDateTime: Enter a valid date with a start and end time.
actions.endBeforeStartSplit: The end time must be after the start time. Split a shift that crosses midnight into two entries.
actions.endBeforeStart: The end time must be after the start time.
actions.tooLong: A single entry cannot be longer than 24 hours.
actions.future: You cannot log time in the future.
actions.tooFarBack: You cannot log time more than {days} days in the past. Ask an administrator to add it.
actions.pickProjectOrTaskEntry: Pick a project or a task for this entry.
actions.entryGoneEdit: That entry no longer exists, or you may not edit it.
actions.onlyOwnEdit: You can only edit your own time.
actions.invoicedNoEdit: This entry has been invoiced and can no longer be changed. Ask an administrator.
actions.entryGoneDelete: That entry no longer exists, or you may not delete it.
actions.onlyOwnDelete: You can only delete your own time.
actions.invoicedNoDelete: This entry has been invoiced and cannot be deleted.

health.title: Portfolio health
health.chartLabel: Portfolio health across {total} projects: {over} over budget, {risk} at risk, {healthy} healthy, {noBudget} without a budget
health.note: Projects by budget burn — logged hours as a share of the budget. Over budget is above 100%, at risk is 85–100%. Projects with no budget set are counted separately, never assumed healthy.

topProjects.title: Where the hours go
topProjects.note: The ten projects with the most hours logged. Length is effort spent, not fee or budget — a long bar can be a large engagement or a small one running over.

burnDonuts.title: Budget burn
burnDonuts.qualifier: TOP 5 BUDGETED PROJECTS BY BURN · ESTIMATES UNDER 10H EXCLUDED AS PLACEHOLDERS
burnDonuts.empty: No projects carry a real budget yet — every estimate on file is below the 10h placeholder floor, so there is no burn to show.
burnDonuts.note: Hours logged against the estimate. The ring fills to 100% and no further, so overruns are told by the centre figure, not the arc — two full red rings are not necessarily equally over.

customerCharts.title: Customers
customerCharts.concentration: {name} alone is {share} of delivered hours and the top five are {top5} — a concentration worth weighing when planning capacity or pricing.
customerCharts.note: Each customer’s share of delivered hours. This measures effort, not fee — rates differ by customer, so the largest slice is not necessarily the largest account.

burnChart.empty: No time has been logged against this project yet.

contract.title: Contract
contract.intro: The hours sales agreed, and the dates they cover. Renewing keeps every previous period on record.
contract.none: No contract terms recorded for this project.
contract.fallback: The budget guard is falling back to the {hours} estimate synced from TrackingTime, which the vendor overwrites on every sync. Record the agreed terms to make the budget stick.
contract.noBudgetToEnforce: There is no budget to enforce, so bookings on it are never refused.

notInstalled.title: Contract terms are not switched on in the database yet, so nobody can record them -- including executives. This is not a permission problem.
notInstalled.apply: Apply <first></first> and then <second></second>, and this panel becomes editable.

contract.noPermission: Contract terms are commercial, so only executives and department heads can record them.
contract.gap: No contract covers today. Period {period} ended on {endsOn}. Hours logged since then sit outside any contract period: they are still recorded, but they cannot be checked against a budget until the renewal is confirmed.
contract.warnNote: Bookings warn from {percent}% and are refused past 100%. Only hours dated inside this period count towards it.
contract.renewIntro: Record the renewed terms once sales confirm them. This adds a new period; period {period} keeps its own budget and the hours already booked against it. The new period must not overlap the old one, so it usually starts the day after it ended.
contract.correctIntro: Correcting a period changes its terms without touching the hours booked against it. Use this for a transcription error, not for a renewal.

history.title: Contract history
history.intro: Every previous term keeps its own budget and its own booked hours. Nothing is overwritten by a renewal.

fields.warnAtHint: Bookings warn from here on. A small retainer and a large programme rarely want the same point.

noColumns.title: No columns yet
noColumns.description: Add a column to start shaping this project's workflow — intake, site visit, report drafted, whatever fits. Columns here are the same groups the list view uses.

actions.denied: You do not have permission to change this project.
actions.noParent: That task is not attached to a project.
actions.sectionNoParent: That column is not attached to a project.

contractActions.denied: Your role does not permit changing contract terms. Contract budgets are commercial terms, so they are limited to executives and department heads.
contractActions.overlap: {hint} Each date can belong to only one contract period, otherwise the budget guard cannot tell which budget applies.
contractActions.overlapHint: That date range overlaps a contract period that already exists on this project.
contractActions.invalid: Those values are not a valid contract: check that the budget is above zero and the end date is not before the start date.
contractActions.duplicate: A contract period with that number already exists on this project. Reload the page and try again.
contractActions.budgetRequired: Enter the agreed budget in hours, above zero.
contractActions.renewalBudgetRequired: Enter the renewed budget in hours, above zero.
contractActions.datesRequired: Enter both contract dates as yyyy-mm-dd.
contractActions.endBeforeStart: The contract cannot end before it starts.
contractActions.renewed: Renewed as contract period {period}: {hours}h from {startsOn} to {endsOn}. The previous period keeps its own budget and the hours booked against it.

budgetPanel.noBudget: No hours budget set for this project, so there is nothing to burn down against. An exec can set one to enable overrun warnings.
